features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures real experience deploying AI systems in production, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, hardening, and failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education the applicant cites as relevant preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent only, with no advanced degree signal.
Master's degree in a relevant technical field.
Doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures hands-on design or ownership of agent-based systems with explicit controls, guardrails, orchestration, and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as shown through concrete engineering problem solving.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Collaborative learning posture
features.description: Captures humility, coachability, and readiness to partner closely with security specialists and other engineers.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers through secure defaults, lower friction, and empathy for internal users.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Engineering rigor and maintainability
features.description: Captures a careful, reliability-minded, maintainable approach to engineering, especially for long-lived or security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives little signal about quality, testing, reliability, or maintainability.
The letter gestures at seriousness or standards, but without concrete habits or practices.
The letter clearly emphasizes dependable systems, testing, maintainability, guardrails, or careful design.
The letter strongly signals security-critical rigor, with explicit habits such as typed or tested tooling, auditable boundaries, reliability-first design, or builder-quality standards.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with mechanisms, examples, outcomes, and observable impact rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on generic claims about being skilled or motivated.
The letter includes some specifics, but they are sparse or vague about mechanism or impact.
The letter gives several concrete examples of what was built, improved, or learned.
The letter repeatedly uses crisp, specific examples that make the applicant's contributions and judgment easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's real production engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Go evidence.
Mentions Go, but without clear depth or ownership.
Shows regular production use of Go in recent work.
Makes Go clearly central, such as a principal language or daily driver tied to sustained backend ownership.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a coherent, memorable, and distinctive story rather than reading like a checklist.

levels.descriptor: Reads as transactional or template-like, with little memorable voice.
Clear and competent but conventional.
Has a noticeable voice or coherent personal arc that helps the reader remember the candidate.
Uses distinctive framing and a well-integrated story that actively strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing adversarial or attacker-minded security practice outside ordinary software engineering duties, especially through CTFs.

levels.descriptor: No adversarial practice outside normal work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional participation or casual practice without depth signals.
The letter shows regular or serious engagement in adversarial exercises.
The letter shows unusually strong external practice, such as near-top finishes or another high-commitment signal.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public codebases through upstream fixes, contribution habits, maintainership, releases, or service to external users.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and self-directed stretch of side projects used as evidence of engineering depth.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational platform or infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: Captures the depth of hands-on professional ownership of production software through tenure, lifecycle breadth, repeated launches, and direct responsibility.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how substantial, central, and production-grade the applicant's Python experience appears.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter connects the applicant's interests and background to this exact role and its stated requirements.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific motivation beyond wanting a software job or a brand-name employer.
Mentions security, scale, or Google in broad terms without a strong personal rationale.
Gives a clear role-relevant reason for interest, such as secure-by-default tooling or scaling scarce security effort.
Presents a precise, memorable thesis for wanting this role that is tightly tied to the team's mandate and the applicant's own priorities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience reviewing systems, designs, or code for security issues and validating remediation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role as scaling scarce security expertise through automation, triage systems, and security-at-scale tooling.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the presence and rigor of formal external security credentials or certifications cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful, role-relevant view of what security engineering is for and why it matters.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related handling of vulnerability reports.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general automation interest, but not with a concrete vulnerability triage example.
Describes a clear example of automating vulnerability intake or routing.
Describes a strong triage automation example with several functions such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, routing, or measurable manual-load reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the mechanical quality of the prose, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and sentence-level professionalism.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors noticeably distract and undermine polish.
Several errors are present, but the letter remains readable.
Only minor errors are present.
The letter is clean and professional throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly align with the recurring constructs above.

levels.descriptor: No security engagement outside day-job claims is shown.
A modest external signal is shown, such as casual CTF participation or a baseline security credential.
A strong external signal is shown, such as serious competitive CTF results or a hands-on credential like OSCP.
Multiple strong external signals are shown, such as both high-level CTF performance and a hands-on offensive certification.
